title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. At the left end its tape is two long blocks of 1s split by a single 0 (0 0 1^1428 0 1^2925 0 1 1); by the time the head reaches the right end, the left part has become a long run of 0s and the right part one long block of 1s (1 1 1 1 0^476 1^3868 0 0).
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps; the C simulator shows none in 109. How the split point moves is not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,363 cells have been visited and 4,240 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At the left-end side switches near 109 steps the tape is 0 0 1^x 0 1^y 0 1 1 (x, y = 1428, 2925 at step 993,152,325; 3993, 327 at step 980,400,468; 1374, 2907 at step 958,686,998); at the right-end switches it is 1 1 1 1 0^u 1^v 0 0 1 1 1 0 (u, v = 3828, 493 at step 980,513,054; 4043, 244 at step 966,274,903).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.34). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.32).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 106 side switches, 4,681,061 steps apart on average (≈ 0.246·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 4362), about 8.1 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.327 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is E reading 1. E is entered only from D reading 0 (which writes 1 and moves left). So a halt is exactly 1 D>0: D on a 0 with a 1 to its left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The shapes above hold at the switches printed; how the split point moves, and why D never stands on a 0 just right of a 1, are open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is two long blocks of 1s at the left end and a long run of 0s plus one block at the right end; each trip across costs about the width squared, for several cells of growth, so the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: Width of the tape at its last extension before step 10<sup>9</sup>.
Side switches in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: Two blocks at one end, a gap and a block at the other
html: The tape at the last side switches:
The sizes jump around; a halt needs D on a 0 just right of a 1.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 106 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 4,681,061 steps apart, which is about 0.246·w2 for the final width w = 4362; each adds about 8.1 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.327.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.34). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.32).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,363 cells (1,385 left of the start, 2,198 right), with a density of 1s of 0.972.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

family: two long blocks of 1s, regrown from one end
summary: At the left end the tape is two long blocks of 1s split by one 0; at the right end, a long run of 0s and one long block of 1s. The split point moves erratically. Width ~ t^(1/3).
